symbols.name: Z_i
symbols.def: The \(i\)-th observation in an iid sample.

symbols.name: mu_P
symbols.def: Designated jointly Borel version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\).

symbols.name: pi_P
symbols.def: Designated jointly Borel conditional Lebesgue-density version of \(A\) given \(X\).

symbols.name: theta_P
symbols.def: The fixed-dose partial mean induced by the designated versions.

symbols.name: T_n
symbols.def: All Borel measurable real-valued estimators based on the sample.

symbols.name: H_beta_free
symbols.def: Four-fold first-order marginal local-polynomial estimator with independent slice-regression and slice-density pilots.

symbols.name: g
symbols.def: Exact covariate-smoothness threshold delivered by the slice-pilot and marginal local-polynomial risk balance.

symbols.name: gOracle
symbols.def: Exact covariate-smoothness threshold delivered by the slice-pilot and marginal local-polynomial risk balance.

symbols.name: Omega
symbols.def: Parameter region on which the explicit beta-free estimator attains the one-dimensional oracle floor.

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: Potential exact polynomial-rate exponent in a region outside \(\Omega\); its existence and any independence from \(\beta\) are not presupposed.

assumptions.condition: For the measurably typed potential-outcome random element \(\mathbf Y\), \(\mathbf Y\perp A\mid X\); equivalently, \(\mathcal L(\mathbf Y\mid A,X)=\mathcal L(\mathbf Y\mid X)\) almost surely.

novel.justification: novel: process-level conditional independence of the measurably typed potential-outcome random element is a recognized strengthening, but it is not the pointwise weak unconfoundedness standard in continuous-dose work and must not be attributed to a source that states only the pointwise form.

assumptions.condition: \(\mu_P:[0,1]\times[0,1]^d\to[-M_Y,M_Y]\) is a jointly Borel-measurable version of \(\mathbb E_P[Y\mid A=a,X=x]\).
\(\pi_P:[0,1]\times[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}\) is a jointly Borel-measurable conditional Lebesgue-density version of \(A\) given \(X\).
\(p_X:[0,1]^d\to[0,\infty)\) is a designated Borel Lebesgue density of \(P_X\).
For every \(x\), \(a\mapsto\mu_P(a,x)\) belongs to the univariate Hölder ball of order \(\alpha\) and radius \(L\).
For every \(x\), \(a\mapsto\pi_P(a\mid x)\) belongs to the univariate Hölder ball of order \(\beta\) and radius \(L\).
\(x\mapsto\mu_P(t_0,x)\) belongs to the coordinatewise \(d\)-variate Hölder ball of order \(s\) and radius \(L\).
\(x\mapsto\pi_P(t_0\mid x)\) belongs to the coordinatewise \(d\)-variate Hölder ball of order \(s\) and radius \(L\).

There exist a standard Borel space \((\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y)\), a \(\mathcal Y\otimes\mathcal B([0,1])/\mathcal B([-M_Y,M_Y])\)-measurable evaluation map \(e:\mathsf Y\times[0,1]\to[-M_Y,M_Y]\), and an \(\mathcal F/\mathcal Y\)-measurable random element \(\mathbf Y\) on the underlying probability space such that \(Y(a)=e(\mathbf Y,a)\) holds for every \(a\in[0,1]\) and at every sample point; that is, the potential-outcome family is the evaluation of \(\mathbf Y\).

novel.justification: novel: the standard-Borel random-element formulation uses standard disintegration machinery, but its explicit use as the causal completion for this singleton-dose proposition is a substantive typing condition rather than routine continuous-dose boilerplate.

definitions.name: Pclass
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)=\{P\in\mathcal P(Z):\text{ there exist designated versions }(\mu_P,\pi_P,p_X)\text{ satisfying }\mathrm{ass:mu-version},\mathrm{ass:pi-version},\mathrm{ass:px-version},\mathrm{ass:bounded-outcome},\mathrm{ass:positivity-lower},\mathrm{ass:positivity-upper},\mathrm{ass:mu-a-holder},\mathrm{ass:pi-a-holder},\mathrm{ass:mu-x-holder},\mathrm{ass:pi-x-holder}\}\). Throughout, a H\"older ball of order \(q>0\) and radius \(L\) means the corresponding H\"older seminorm ball: \(L\) bounds all required positive-order coordinate derivatives and the terminal H\"older modulus or Taylor remainder, but it does not bound the zeroth-order supremum norm. For \(0<q<1\), this is the \(q\)-H\"older modulus of the function itself; for \(q\in\mathbb N\), the usual bounded \(q\)-th-derivative convention applies; the \(x\)-conditions are coordinatewise. Function values are controlled separately by the outcome-envelope and positivity assumptions. The parameter domain is \(M_Y,L>0\), \(0<c\le1\), \(t_0\in(0,1)\), \(\alpha,\beta,s>0\), and \(d\ge1\); thus \(t_0\) has a two-sided neighbourhood inside \([0,1]\).

definitions.name: P_0
definitions.construction: \(X\sim\mathrm{Unif}([0,1]^d),\ A\mid X\sim\mathrm{Unif}([0,1]),\ Y=0,\ Y(a)=0\) for every \(a\in[0,1]\), with designated versions \(p_X(x)=1\), \(\pi_{P_0}(a\mid x)=1\), and \(\mu_{P_0}(a,x)=0\).

definitions.name: M_n
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)=\inf_{\widehat\theta\in\mathfrak T_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\theta-\theta_P(t_0))^2]\), where the supremum is over the nonempty class certified by \(\mathrm{prop:class-nonempty}\).

definitions.name: H_beta_free
definitions.construction:
Fix a bounded nonnegative kernel \(K\), supported on \([-1,1]\) and bounded below on a neighbourhood of zero. Put \(p=\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\), \(S(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top\), \(K_h(a)=h^{-1}K((a-t_0)/h)\), and \(S_h(a)=S((a-t_0)/h)\). Deterministically split the sample into four disjoint folds \(I_\mu,I_{\mathrm{aux}},I_X,I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), each of size proportional to \(n\). Partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\mu j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\mu\), with the number of cells \(J_\mu\le C_d'\delta_\mu^{-d}\). On \(I_\mu\), for \(x\in B_{\mu j}\), define
\[
\widehat\mu_0(x)=
\frac{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}Y_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
{\sum_{i\in I_\mu}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\mu j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\mu\}}
\]
when the denominator is positive and set it to zero otherwise. Independently partition \([0,1]^d\) by a deterministic regular grid into Borel cells \(B_{\pi j}\) of diameter at most \(C_d\delta_\pi\), with the number of cells \(J_\pi\le C_d'\delta_\pi^{-d}\). On \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), let \(N_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j}\}\), \(R_{\pi j}=\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{aux}}}\mathbf 1\{X_i\in B_{\pi j},\ |A_i-t_0|\le b_\pi\}\), and, for \(x\in B_{\pi j}\), define
\[
\widehat\pi_0(x)=\operatorname{clip}_{[c/2,2/c]}\left\{\frac{R_{\pi j}}{2b_\pi(N_{\pi j}\vee1)}\right\}.
\]
Extend both pilots constantly in dose: \(\widehat\mu(a,x)=\widehat\mu_0(x)\) and \(\widehat\pi(a\mid x)=\widehat\pi_0(x)\). On the independent fold \(I_X\), define \(\widehat m(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\mu(a,X_\ell)\) and \(\widehat f(a)=|I_X|^{-1}\sum_{\ell\in I_X}\widehat\pi(a\mid X_\ell)\). For \(i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}\), put
\[
\widehat\xi_i=\frac{\widehat f(A_i)}{\widehat\pi(A_i\mid X_i)}\{Y_i-\widehat\mu(A_i,X_i)\}+\widehat m(A_i).
\]
With \(N_{\mathrm{lp}}=|I_{\mathrm{lp}}|\), define
\[
\widehat D_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)^\top,
\qquad
\widehat R_h=N_{\mathrm{lp}}^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_{\mathrm{lp}}}K_h(A_i)S_h(A_i)\widehat\xi_i.
\]
Set
\[
\lambda_*=\frac c2\lambda_{\min}\left\{\int_{-1}^1K(u)S(u)S(u)^\top\,du\right\}>0.
\]
The estimator family is
\[
\widehat\theta_{h,b_\mu,\delta_\mu,b_\pi,\delta_\pi}
=\operatorname{clip}_{[-M_Y,M_Y]}\left[e_0^\top\widehat D_h^{-1}\widehat R_h\,\mathbf 1\{\lambda_{\min}(\widehat D_h)\ge\lambda_*\}\right],
\]
where the bracketed value is defined as zero on the bad-Gram event. Require \(b_\mu,b_\pi\le\min(t_0,1-t_0)\). Counts, clipping, eigenvalues, inversion on the good-Gram set, and the assigned bad-event value make the map Borel measurable.

definitions.name: gOracle
definitions.construction:
Put \(A_0=\alpha\wedge1\), \(B_0=\beta\wedge1\), \(C_0=2\alpha+1\), \(\ell=(\alpha-B_0)_+\), and \(I=[\ell,A_0]\). For \(z\in I\), define
\[
D_\mu(z)=C_0-\frac{z}{A_0}-2z,
\qquad
D_\pi(z)=C_0-\frac{\alpha-z}{B_0}-2(\alpha-z).
\]
On the structural domain \(A_0+B_0\ge\alpha\), the separated-pilot threshold is
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)
=
\min_{\substack{z\in I:\ D_\mu(z)>0,\ D_\pi(z)>0}}
\max\left\{
\frac{dz}{D_\mu(z)},
\frac{d(\alpha-z)}{D_\pi(z)}
\right\}.
\]
This one-dimensional optimization has the following closed form. Let
\[
\Delta=\frac1{A_0}-\frac1{B_0},
\qquad
z_c=
\begin{cases}
\alpha/2,&\Delta=0,\\[2mm]
\displaystyle
\frac{2\alpha C_0}{2C_0+\alpha\Delta+\sqrt{4C_0^2+\alpha^2\Delta^2}},&\Delta\ne0,
\end{cases}
\]
and put \(z_*=\min\{A_0,\max\{\ell,z_c\}\}\). The denominators \(D_\mu(z_*)\) and \(D_\pi(z_*)\) are positive, and
\[
g(\alpha,\beta,d)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \frac{d\ell}{D_\mu(\ell)},&z_c<\ell,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{dz_c}{D_\mu(z_c)}
=\frac{d(\alpha-z_c)}{D_\pi(z_c)},&\ell\le z_c\le A_0,\\[3mm]
\displaystyle \frac{d(\alpha-A_0)}{D_\pi(A_0)},&z_c>A_0.
\end{cases}
\]
The adjacent expressions agree when \(z_c=\ell\) or \(z_c=A_0\).

definitions.name: Omega
definitions.construction:
The first-order separated-pilot oracle region is
\[
\Omega
=
\left\{(\alpha,\beta,s,d):
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\quad s\wedge1\ge g(\alpha,\beta,d)
\right\}.
\]

statements.statement: For every admissible \(M_Y,L,c,t_0,\alpha,\beta,s,d\), the witness \(P_0\) belongs to \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\). Its displayed designated versions satisfy the version convention, including the Hölder convention, and hence the minimax supremum is over a nonempty set.
statements.justification: The uniform \(X\), uniform \(A\), zero-outcome law satisfies every version, positivity, envelope, and smoothness condition under the frozen Hölder convention.
statements.gap: This is a model-coherence certificate, not a rate result.
statements.consumer: It makes the minimax supremum nonempty for every declared tuple.

statements.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\), \(\theta_P(t_0)=\int\mu_P(t_0,x)p_X(x)dx\) is well defined and independent of the admissible designated versions: any two such regression versions agree \(P_X\)-almost everywhere at \(t_0\), because positivity upgrades conditional almost-everywhere agreement and the designated treatment-direction versions are continuous.
statements.justification: The pointwise target must not depend on the representative selected to define smoothness.
statements.gap: Pointwise dose-response work usually states regularity for a chosen regression version without proving target invariance across admissible versions.
statements.consumer: It licenses the loss in the minimax functional.

statements.statement:
For every \(0<\beta<\beta^{\prime}<\infty\) and every admissible \(\alpha,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0\) such that the rough tuple satisfies \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\), there are \(0<C_{\mathrm{low}}\le C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty\) and \(n_0\in\mathbb N\), none depending on \(n\), such that for every \(n\ge n_0\),
\[
C_{\mathrm{low}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le \mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\le C_{\mathrm{up}}n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
1\le
\frac{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}{\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta^{\prime},s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}
\le \frac{C_{\mathrm{up}}}{C_{\mathrm{low}}}.
\]
No oracle-region condition on \(\beta^{\prime}\) is required.
statements.justification: Class nesting, the rough-class oracle upper bound, and the all-\(\beta\) lower floor give constant-factor equivalence.
statements.gap: No corresponding exact equivalence is proved for fixed \(0<c<1\) when the rough tuple lies outside \(\Omega\).
statements.consumer: It states precisely where treatment-density smoothness may be omitted from first-order minimax exponent calculations.

statements.statement: Suppose \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\). Then for every admissible \(M_Y,L,c,t_0\), there are \(0<C_-\le C_+<\infty\), independent of \(n\), such that \[C_-r_n(\alpha)\le\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\le C_+r_n(\alpha).\] On this oracle region, if \(\beta<\alpha\), the same-class minimax exponent \(2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)\) is numerically larger than the exponent \(2\beta/(2\beta+1)\) obtained by balancing the treatment-smoothing component of Bonvini and Kennedy's conditional estimator-risk bound with its leading variance order. The models and guarantees differ: the present result is a uniform minimax statement over the displayed class, whereas theirs is a conditional bound for a specified estimator. This is a contrast between unlike guarantees, not a strict tightening or estimator-domination claim.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\). Lemma~\texttt{lem:oracle-region-tuning} supplies deterministic bandwidths and grid widths in Definition~\texttt{def:beta-free-handle} for which Lemma~\texttt{lem:localized-polynomial-master-risk} gives, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)}
\mathbb E_P[(\widehat\theta-\theta_P(t_0))^2]
\le C_+^0r_n(\alpha).
\]
Definition~\texttt{def:beta-free-handle} makes \(\widehat\theta\) a Borel measurable function of the sample, so it belongs to \(\mathfrak T_n\). Taking the infimum in Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-mse} proves the upper bound for sufficiently large \(n\). For the finitely many remaining sample sizes, the zero estimator has risk at most \(M_Y^2\); enlarging \(C_+^0\) to a finite constant \(C_+\) extends the upper inequality to every \(n\). Lemma~\texttt{lem:all-beta-oracle-lower-floor} gives a constant \(C_->0\), independent of \(n\), for which
\[
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\ge C_-r_n(\alpha).
\]
Enlarging \(C_+\) if necessary gives \(C_-\le C_+\), proving the exact order.

For the numerical comparison, suppose \(\beta<\alpha\). Then \(\alpha\wedge\beta=\beta\), and strict monotonicity of \(x\mapsto2x/(2x+1)\) gives
\[
\frac{2\alpha}{2\alpha+1}>
\frac{2\beta}{2\beta+1}
=\frac{2(\alpha\wedge\beta)}{2(\alpha\wedge\beta)+1}.
\]
Lemma~\texttt{lem:bonvini-kennedy-treatment-smoothing-bound} records that the number on the right is obtained by balancing \(h^\beta\), the treatment-smoothing component of Bonvini and Kennedy's conditional estimator-risk bound, with its leading variance order \((nh)^{-1}\). The two guarantees are unlike: the present theorem is a uniform minimax statement over \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)\), whereas their result is a conditional risk bound for a specified higher-order estimator under its own conditions. The displayed inequality is therefore a numerical contrast; it proves neither a strict tightening of their theorem nor domination of their estimator.
statements.justification: The explicit four-fold estimator and its deterministic tuning attain the one-dimensional pointwise H\"older rate on \(\Omega\), while the uniform-treatment Le Cam submodel supplies the matching lower bound. The closest internal comparator, \texttt{stat\_dose\_response\_minimax\_holder\_anisotropic\_converse/thm:sharp-pointwise-lower-bound}, proves the all-\(\beta\) lower floor on its own class but is lower-bound-only; its companion results leave the corresponding same-class upper questions undischarged. The banked class requires a H\"older-\(s\) bounded-above covariate density and local positivity, and its theorems additionally assume baseline-submodel slack, whereas the present class permits an arbitrary Borel covariate density and imposes global two-sided treatment-density bounds. Since neither class contains the other, this theorem supplies an analogous constructive matching upper bound and exact two-sided order on the present class over the computable region \(\Omega\), not a completion of the banked result. Bonvini--Kennedy is the closest published continuous-dose estimator-risk comparator; squaring its absolute treatment-smoothing bias \(h^\beta\) before balancing with \((nh)^{-1}\) gives the numerical exponent \(2\beta/(2\beta+1)\).
statements.gap: For fixed \(0<c<1\), the theorem does not characterize the complement of \(\Omega\), where the exact exponent remains the declared open question. Class incomparability means it also does not discharge the accepted-bank prior's same-class upper endpoint. It neither orders estimator risks under identical assumptions nor provides the pointwise inference conclusions of Kennedy--Ma--McHugh--Small, Colangelo--Lee, or Takatsu--Westling; the integrated-risk RKHS or Sobolev theory of Kim--Wang; the binary-treatment CATE frontier of Kennedy--Balakrishnan--Robins--Wasserman; or the distinct incremental-effect and data-fusion targets of Schindl--Shen--Kennedy and Lim--Luedtke.
statements.consumer: Continuous-exposure software receives an explicit estimator, tuning certificate, and computable regime for attaining the oracle pointwise MSE rate. The surrounding results identify the remaining field-level increments: Lemma~\texttt{lem:all-beta-oracle-lower-floor} independently supplies the present-class floor, Theorem~\texttt{thm:beta-invariance} gives the nested-class \(\beta\) comparison on \(\Omega\), and Lemma~\texttt{lem:extreme-low-s-fuzzy-lower} gives the low-smoothness converse exponent \(8/\{4+2/(\alpha\vee\beta)+d/s\}\). Bank-side coverage is complete because no other accepted-bank entry studies the continuous fixed-dose partial mean.

statements.statement:
Fix \(0<c<1\). For parameter tuples in either residual region
\[
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)<\alpha
\]
or
\[
(\alpha\wedge1)+(\beta\wedge1)\ge\alpha,
\qquad s\wedge1<g(\alpha,\beta,d),
\]
does there exist an exact polynomial-rate exponent \(\rho(\alpha,\beta,s,d)\) such that
\[
\mathcal M_n(\alpha,\beta,s,d,M_Y,L,c,t_0)
\asymp n^{-\rho(\alpha,\beta,s,d)}?
\]
If so, what is that exponent and in which subregions, if any, is it independent of \(\beta\)?

sampling_model.design: The statistical experiment consists of \(n\) iid observations \(Z_i=(Y_i,A_i,X_i)\), with bounded outcomes, continuous treatment on \([0,1]\), covariates on \([0,1]^d\), designated measurable regression and density versions, and uniform two-sided treatment-density bounds \(c\le\pi_P(a\mid x)\le1/c\). The model imposes treatment-direction H\"older orders \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) and covariate-direction order \(s\) at the interior point \(t_0\), but no smoothness or lower bound on the covariate density.
sampling_model.overlap: In the frozen class, \(c\le\pi_P(a\mid x)\le1/c\). At the DEGENERATE BOUNDARY CORNER \(c=1\), these inequalities force \(\pi_P(a\mid x)=1\), equivalently uniform \(A\) independent of \(X\). This degeneracy is unavailable at fixed \(0<c<1\) and supplies no solution of the deficient-frontier open question.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The achieving estimator estimates \(\mu_P(t_0,\cdot)\) by a bounded slice regressogram on \(I_\mu\), estimates \(\pi_P(t_0\mid\cdot)\) independently on \(I_{\mathrm{aux}}\), empirically marginalizes both pilots on \(I_X\), and fits a marginal degree-\(\lfloor\alpha\rfloor\) local polynomial on \(I_{\mathrm{lp}}\). These tuning and splitting choices are estimator-side hypotheses, not member properties of \(\mathcal P\).
sampling_model.causal_interpretation: The minimax analysis targets the observed-data functional \(\theta_P(t_0)=\int\mu_P(t_0,x)p_X(x)\,dx\). Its interpretation as \(\mathbb E[Y(t_0)]\) is a separate conclusion available only under Proposition~\texttt{prop:causal-identification-at-t0} and its stated causal and continuity conditions.

target_estimand: \(\theta_P(t_0)=\int\mu_P(t_0,x)p_X(x)\,dx\), the observed-data fixed-dose partial mean; under Proposition~\texttt{prop:causal-identification-at-t0}, \(\theta_P(t_0)=\mathbb E[Y(t_0)]\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The accepted theorem proves the all-\(\beta\) lower floor \(n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}\) on \(\mathcal P_{\alpha,\beta,s}(M,c_0,\epsilon_0,t_0)\), under baseline-submodel slack, H\"older-\(s\) bounded-above \(p_X\), and local positivity; its smooth-covariate benchmark is \(s\ge d/4\), and it leaves the deficient-regime same-class upper frontier unresolved. Its class and the present class are incomparable because the present class allows arbitrary Borel \(p_X\) but requires global two-sided treatment-density bounds.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Lemma~\texttt{lem:all-beta-oracle-lower-floor} independently reproduces the rate shape for the present incomparable class; Theorem~\texttt{thm:oracle-high-s} newly supplies the constructive matching upper bound on \(\Omega\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 conditionally bounds a specified higher-order estimator with treatment-smoothing bias term \(h^{\alpha\wedge\beta}\) and leading variance order \((nh)^{-1}\). It is an estimator-specific conditional-risk theorem, not a uniform minimax-MSE theorem over the present H\"older class.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: When \(\beta<\alpha\), Theorem~\texttt{thm:oracle-high-s} has the numerically larger exponent \(2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)\), whereas balancing the cited treatment-smoothing component with \((nh)^{-1}\) gives \(2\beta/(2\beta+1)\). Because the models and guarantees differ, this is an informed numerical contrast, not a strict tightening or estimator-domination claim.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives an asymptotically linear expansion and a \(\sqrt{nh}\)-Gaussian limit for a debiased local-linear estimator of the same fixed-dose partial mean under Conditions A1--A5, including twice continuous differentiability of the partial mean, a positive Lipschitz marginal treatment density, and high-level nuisance rates. It is a pointwise limit-law theorem, not a uniform H\"older-class minimax-MSE result or a nested conditional-density-smoothness comparison.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Theorem~\texttt{thm:oracle-high-s} addresses worst-case minimax MSE on \(\Omega\), while Theorem~\texttt{thm:beta-invariance} supplies the nested \(\beta\)-class equivalence there; neither theorem claims Takatsu--Westling's inference conclusion.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 gives pointwise error \(O_P\{(nh)^{-1/2}+h^2+r_n(t_0)s_n(t_0)\}\) for its local-linear pseudo-outcome estimator under uniform-norm nuisance convergence, at least one correctly specified nuisance, bounded inverse propensity, bounded nuisance classes with finite uniform entropy integrals, a compact symmetric kernel, \(h\to0\), \(nh^3\to\infty\), and twice-smooth effect and marginal-density conditions. Theorem 3 further assumes \(r_n(t_0)s_n(t_0)=o_P\{(nh)^{-1/2}\}\) for its Gaussian limit. These are estimator-specific pointwise and limit results, not uniform H\"older-class minimax-MSE bounds.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Definition~\texttt{def:beta-free-handle} and Theorem~\texttt{thm:oracle-high-s} replace externally assumed nuisance rates and entropy control with explicit separated regressogram pilots whose \(L_2(P_X)\) risks are proved uniformly; four-fold independence removes the empirical-process condition, and the finite-sample envelope yields a minimax upper bound on \(\Omega\). The present estimator does not inherit misspecification-style double robustness and uses stronger global two-sided positivity.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 3.1 gives asymptotic linearity and normality for cross-fitted kernel DML under partial-\(L_2\) nuisance consistency and the high-level product condition \(\sqrt{nh^{d_T}}\,\lVert\widehat f-f\rVert\,\lVert\widehat\gamma-\gamma\rVert=o_P(1)\), with at least one nuisance correct, treatment-direction differentiability, a second-order differentiable kernel, \(h\to0\), \(nh^{d_T}\to\infty\), and \(nh^{d_T+4}\to C\). It is an inference theorem, not a uniform minimax-risk theorem.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Definition~\texttt{def:beta-free-handle} and Theorem~\texttt{thm:oracle-high-s} discharge nuisance performance through a concrete estimator and prove worst-case MSE on \(\Omega\), uniformly over arbitrary Borel \(p_X\). This is a different conclusion from Colangelo--Lee's high-level-rate inference result, not a claim that their theorem assumes smooth \(p_X\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1 and 2 give, respectively, a H\"older-model minimax lower bound for binary-treatment CATE at a covariate point and a matching local-polynomial higher-order upper result under their stated attainability conditions. The lower bound uses localized fuzzy hypotheses. The treatment is binary, the target is a conditional average treatment effect rather than an interior fixed-dose partial mean, and the model has no continuous treatment-density smoothness coordinate \(\beta\).
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: Theorem~\texttt{thm:oracle-high-s} proves the one-dimensional oracle MSE exponent for the interior fixed-dose partial mean on \(\Omega\). Lemma~\texttt{lem:extreme-low-s-fuzzy-lower} adapts the standard fuzzy-hypothesis method to the present continuous-dose class and obtains \(r_{\mathrm f}=8/\{4+2/(\alpha\vee\beta)+d/s\}\), strictly strengthening the oracle floor when \(d/s>4+4/\alpha-2/(\alpha\vee\beta)\). The novelty claim concerns this construction and exponent, not the fuzzy-hypothesis technique.

tldr: On the explicit separated-pilot oracle region \(\Omega\), the four-fold marginal local-polynomial estimator attains the pointwise minimax mean-squared-error rate \(n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}\), matching a one-dimensional Le Cam lower submodel whose treatment density is uniform. When \(\beta<\alpha\), this exponent is numerically larger than the exponent \(2\beta/(2\beta+1)\) obtained from Bonvini and Kennedy's treatment-smoothing bias--variance balance: their \(h^\beta\) term is an absolute bias, so the MSE balance is \(h^{2\beta}\asymp(nh)^{-1}\). The comparison is between unlike guarantees and is not an estimator-domination claim.

project_justification.gap: Existing continuous-dose results can display treatment-density smoothness in estimator-specific conditional risk bounds, while the fixed-dose partial-mean minimax frontier over nested anisotropic H\"older classes is not thereby determined. In particular, an absolute treatment-smoothing bias \(h^{\alpha\wedge\beta}\) contributes its square to mean-squared error. Outside the explicit region \(\Omega\), the exact frontier remains unresolved for \(0<c<1\), although the core records an optimized achievable bracket, an all-\(\beta\) oracle lower floor, and a stronger fuzzy lower bound in an extreme low-\(s\) region.
project_justification.niche: The note studies the interior fixed-dose partial mean \(\theta_P(t_0)\) under strict positivity, separating the causal identifying functional from the statistical minimax problem. Its main closed regime is \(\Omega\), determined by the exact feasibility threshold for two independent slice pilots and marginal local-polynomial smoothing; it also isolates the boundary \(c=1\), where the oracle rate holds without an \(x\)-smoothness requirement.
project_justification.fill: The explicit Borel estimator has uniform risk at most a constant times \(n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}\) on \(\Omega\), and a uniform-treatment two-point submodel gives the matching lower bound for every finite \(\beta\). Nested-class monotonicity then yields one-sided \(\beta\)-invariance comparisons whenever the rougher tuple lies in \(\Omega\). The paper reports the deficient-region upper and lower brackets honestly rather than promoting them to an exact rate.

related_work:
Three sources are closest to the theorem-level rate claim, but none proves the present result. First, Bonvini and Kennedy analyze a specified higher-order continuous-dose estimator conditionally on nuisance training. Their Theorem 3.1 contains absolute treatment-smoothing bias \(h^{\alpha\wedge\beta}\) and leading variance order \((nh)^{-1}\). When \(\beta<\alpha\), squaring that bias and balancing \(h^{2\beta}\) with \((nh)^{-1}\) gives the numerical exponent \(2\beta/(2\beta+1)\), whereas Theorem~\texttt{thm:oracle-high-s} proves the uniform same-class minimax exponent \(2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)\) on \(\Omega\). The assumptions and guarantees are different, so this is not a tightening of their theorem or domination of their estimator. Second, Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman give matching H\"older-model minimax rates and an elbow for binary-treatment CATE. That is the closest sharp causal minimax analogue, but binary treatment has no continuous conditional-density smoothness index \(\beta\), and CATE at a covariate point is not the interior fixed-dose partial mean. Third, Kim and Wang give upper theory requiring no conditional-treatment-density estimation and a matching Sobolev lower bound for two-stage kernel ridge regression. Their loss is integrated MISE for an entire continuous-treatment curve over RKHS or Sobolev source classes under relative overlap; it is not pointwise MSE at \(t_0\) over the present anisotropic H\"older class. Their result therefore neither proves nor rules out nested-class \(\beta\)-invariance here.

The remaining continuous-treatment papers are closer in estimand or estimator architecture than in minimax conclusion. Kennedy, Ma, McHugh, and Small develop kernel-smoothed doubly robust estimation of the continuous-treatment curve, with pointwise error and Gaussian limits under nuisance-rate and empirical-process conditions; they do not give a uniform minimax MSE theorem over the present class. Colangelo and Lee use kernel localization, orthogonal moments, and cross-fitting for double-debiased inference on dose-response functions and partial effects; their conclusion is asymptotic inference under high-level nuisance product rates, not an explicit-pilot minimax bound. Takatsu and Westling study the same fixed-dose partial mean and establish a pointwise asymptotically linear expansion and Gaussian limit under local smoothness and high-level nuisance conditions; that is the nearest target-level inference comparator, but it does not compare minimax risks across \(\beta\)-indexed classes. Schindl, Shen, and Kennedy study incremental continuous-exposure effects designed for settings in which ordinary fixed-dose targets encounter positivity difficulties; their tilted intervention functional is not \(\theta_P(t_0)\), so their efficiency and rate results do not answer the present fixed-dose question. Lim and Luedtke develop a Neyman-orthogonal loss for dose-response learning with partially aligned multi-source data; their data-fusion experiment and curve-learning objective differ from the ordinary iid pointwise minimax experiment here.

Two further lines supply methodology or a different notion of difficulty rather than a direct comparator. Robins, Li, Tchetgen Tchetgen, and van der Vaart develop higher-order influence functions and higher-order \(U\)-statistics for nonlinear functional estimation; this is methodological substrate for higher-order correction, not a continuous-dose theorem with the present target, class, and loss. Liu, Mukherjee, Robins, and Tchetgen Tchetgen study adaptive nonparametric functional estimation through second-order \(U\)-statistics and finite-dimensional approximation; they do not establish the oracle-region pointwise dose-response rate or a treatment-density-smoothness comparison. Balakrishnan, Kennedy, and Wasserman characterize limits of structure-agnostic black-box functional estimation; those bounds intentionally omit the H\"older structure exploited here and therefore do not determine this structured minimax frontier. Finally, Tsybakov supplies the standard H\"older, concentration, and minimax lower-bound toolkit used as mathematical substrate, rather than a causal-dose-response comparator.

The accepted-bank fixed-dose result \texttt{stat\_dose\_response\_minimax\_holder\_anisotropic\_converse/thm:sharp-pointwise-lower-bound} is the closest internal theorem-level prior. Among the six auditable comparator rows, it and Bonvini--Kennedy are the two closest to the precise field-level increment supplied by Theorem~\texttt{thm:oracle-high-s}; the three published sources identified at the start remain the closest published rate comparators as a group. The banked theorem proves the all-\(\beta\) pointwise lower floor \(n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}\) on its own class, with smooth-covariate benchmark \(s\ge d/4\). Its companion results \texttt{stat\_dose\_response\_minimax\_holder\_anisotropic\_converse/thm:sharp-minimax-smooth-covariate} and \texttt{stat\_dose\_response\_minimax\_holder\_anisotropic\_converse/thm:frontier-bracket-deficient} expressly leave, respectively, the matching same-class upper bound and the deficient-regime same-class upper endpoint undischarged. The banked core's only upper-side object is a cited conditional Bonvini--Kennedy comparator rather than a same-class upper theorem, so the prior is lower-bound-only. The class difference and the theorem-level assumption difference are separate: the banked class imposes a H\"older-\(s\) bounded-above covariate density and local positivity, its theorems additionally assume baseline-submodel slack, and the present class instead allows an arbitrary Borel covariate density while imposing global two-sided treatment-density bounds. Neither class contains the other. Consequently, Theorem~\texttt{thm:oracle-high-s} does not discharge the banked prior's same-class upper endpoint. It supplies the analogous constructive matching upper bound on the present incomparable class over the explicitly computable region \(\Omega\), and hence exact two-sided order there; this advances the same question without completing the banked theorem. The remaining increments are, in order, that Lemma~\texttt{lem:all-beta-oracle-lower-floor} independently reproduces the floor's rate shape for the present incomparable class, Theorem~\texttt{thm:beta-invariance} adds the nested-class \(\beta\) comparison on \(\Omega\), and Lemma~\texttt{lem:extreme-low-s-fuzzy-lower} contributes the converse exponent \(8/\{4+2/(\alpha\vee\beta)+d/s\}\), which is strictly stronger than the oracle floor exactly when \(d/s>4+4/\alpha-2/(\alpha\vee\beta)\). What is not delivered is equally explicit: for \(0<c<1\) outside \(\Omega\), the exact exponent remains undetermined and is the note's declared open question. Bank-side coverage is complete: no other accepted-bank entry targets the continuous fixed-dose partial mean; the remaining statistical entries concern a discrete-ATE logarithmic-gap match, a differentially private CATE result, or a policy-regret margin-and-overlap result.
interpretation: Within \(\Omega\), treatment-density smoothness does not determine the minimax exponent: the lower submodel already has a uniform treatment density, and the explicit estimator reaches the one-dimensional treatment-smoothing floor. The condition \((\alpha,\beta,s,d)\in\Omega\) is an achievability regime for the present separated-pilot construction, not a claim that estimation outside it must depend on \(\beta\). At \(c=1\), normalization and the two-sided positivity bounds force the treatment density to equal one, and the oracle exponent holds for every \(s\) and \(\beta\).
technical_internal_limitation: For \(0<c<1\), the exact polynomial exponent is not characterized on the complement of \(\Omega\). The available first-order construction yields an explicit parameterized upper exponent, while the all-\(\beta\) oracle floor and the extreme-low-\(s\) fuzzy construction yield lower bounds that need not match it. The prescribed full-rank projection route also encounters a dimension obstruction in part of the low-\(s\) region, although that counting obstruction does not rule out ridge, pseudoinverse, rare-cell, or other stabilized procedures.
honest_scope: The proved exact-order claim is \(\mathcal M_n\asymp n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+1)}\) on \(\Omega\), together with the special boundary result at \(c=1\). The nested-class theorem compares finite \(\beta<\beta'\) when the rougher tuple lies in \(\Omega\); it does not establish global \(\beta\)-invariance for all \(s\), does not resolve the deficient frontier, and does not supply a limit law or Wald inference. The Bonvini--Kennedy comparison is numerical and componentwise, with the bias squared before MSE balancing; it is not a strict improvement theorem for their estimator.
